g1|variants|quantity contract.summary: A quantity contract is a binding long-term sales agreement where a customer commits to purchasing a specific total quantity of material over a defined validity period. Variants differ by pricing determination, fulfillment mechanics with or without subsequent delivery creation, and release order integration.

variants.name: Standard Quantity Contract with Delivery
variants.when_used: Standard long-term agreement where releases are processed via sales orders leading to outbound deliveries and billing.
variants.key_config: Sales document type MK configured with item category KMN, schedule line category CN, and standard copy control routines from contract to release order (VA01) and delivery (VL01N).

variants.name: Value-Quant Mixed Quantity Contract
variants.when_used: Agreements combining target quantity constraints with specific value limits or multi-material assortment rules.
variants.key_config: Value contract item category WVN with specific target quantity verification active in incompletion procedures and pricing reference material assignments.

variants.name: Quantity Contract without Delivery (Direct Billing)
variants.when_used: Agreements where contract releases or direct service executions bypass shipping and bill directly from the order or contract state.
values: A (Delivery-related - no goods receipt) or B
variants.key_config: Item category KMQ configured for order-related billing, setting billing relevance to A or B, omitting delivery requirement in copy control.

variants.name: Intercompany Quantity Contract Fulfillment
variants.when_used: Global framework agreements managed by a sales organization in one company code fulfilled by a plant in another company code.
variants.key_config: Intercompany billing type IV/PI assigned, delivering plant mapped to external company code, and customer master data maintained for intercompany partner function (PI).

g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.title: Standard Quantity Contract with Delivery
g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.story: Imagine a giant balloon factory that promises to sell a customer a thousand water balloons over the year, writing down the exact number on a special agreement scroll so neither side forgets. In SAP S/4HANA, a Quantity Contract (sales document type MK) is a legal pre-sale agreement where a customer commits to purchase a specific total quantity of material within a defined validity period, serving as the master outline from which subsequent release orders, outbound deliveries, and delivery-related billings are drawn.
g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.why_business_needs_it: This scenario allows businesses to lock in long-term customer commitments and secure guaranteed sales volume while offering tiered pricing and streamlined fulfillment. It prevents administrative overhead by avoiding the creation of independent sales orders from scratch every time the customer needs a partial shipment.

modules.role: Manages contract creation (MK), pricing conditions, release order creation, and downstream delivery-related billing.
modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) for outbound delivery processing and picking/packing.

modules.role: Controls outbound delivery creation, shipping point determination, picking, and Goods Issue posting against the release order.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for revenue recognition and customer invoicing.

modules.role: Processes billing documents generated from deliveries, posts revenue, and manages customer receivables.
modules.hands_off_to: SD to update billing status back onto the document flow.

g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.title: Value-Quant Mixed Quantity Contract (Quantity Contract WK1)
g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.story:
Imagine a giant toy store agrees to buy one thousand toy cars over the year, and you promise to lock in a special low price for that whole batch. In SAP, this agreement is captured in a special sales document called a quantity contract, which tracks how many cars the customer has ordered so far against their total limit. When the customer is ready for some cars, you create regular sales orders referencing that contract, and the system automatically checks that they do not buy more than their agreed limit. This specific variant, the Value-Quant Mixed Quantity Contract (contract type WK1 with item category WVN), ties the target quantity and value checks to a pricing reference material while billing based on outbound deliveries.

A Quantity Contract (Sales Document Type WK1) is a legal binding agreement where a customer commits to purchase a specific quantity or value of materials within a defined validity period, acting as an outline agreement that absorbs subsequent release orders (calls-off) up to the target quantity, utilizing delivery-related billing (Billing Relevance F).
g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.why_business_needs_it: Businesses use quantity contracts to secure long-term customer commitments and offer tiered pricing while managing fulfillment and credit control through subsequent deliveries. It prevents unauthorized discounting by binding release orders directly to the agreed framework agreement terms.

g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.title: Quantity Contract without Delivery (Direct Billing)
g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.story: Imagine a giant agreement where a customer promises to buy a specific total quantity of items over a year, and instead of shipping every little piece with a delivery document, the company just bills the customer directly as orders roll in. In SAP S/4HANA Sales, a quantity contract (document type MK) holds this target quantity, and subsequent sales orders or direct billing documents draw down against that target without requiring a Logistics Execution outbound delivery.
g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.why_business_needs_it: This setup allows businesses to lock in long-term sales commitments and volume targets with major clients while streamlining the billing process for services or goods where formal warehouse delivery documents add unnecessary administrative overhead. It guarantees accurate quantity tracking against the contract release without triggering inventory movements or warehouse tasks.

g1|core|quantity contract|intercompany q.title: Intercompany Quantity Contract Fulfillment
g1|core|quantity contract|intercompany q.story: Imagine a giant toy store group where one company sells the toys, but another company actually ships them from a different warehouse. In SAP, we set up an Intercompany Quantity Contract so a customer can sign a legally binding deal for a total number of items, and the supplying company handles the deliveries and billing across company codes automatically. This orchestrates multi-company trade without manual paperwork every time an order arrives.
g1|core|quantity contract|intercompany q.why_business_needs_it: Large corporate enterprises require intercompany sales execution to legally separate selling entities from manufacturing or distributing plants across different company codes. The quantity contract establishes binding target quantities and prices, while the intercompany workflow automates cross-company delivery and intercompany billing.

modules.role: Manages the intercompany quantity contract (MK), subsequent sales orders, outbound deliveries, and customer/intercompany billing documents.
modules.hands_off_to: MM (Materials Management) for stock check and LE for delivery execution.

modules.role: Handles shipping point determination, picking, packing, and goods issue processing for the supplying plant.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for goods movement postings and billing revenue recognition.

modules.role: Posts customer receivables, intercompany payables/receivables between company codes, and general ledger entries.

config_steps.values: Sales Org: 1000; Dist.Channel: 10; Division: 00; Plant: 2000; Intercompany Customer: C2000
config_steps.check: Run VF01 for an intercompany billing document and verify that customer C2000 is billed as the ordering party.
config_steps.why: This assignment links the supplying plant to the internal customer representing the selling company code for intercompany billing.
config_steps.if_missing: If missing, intercompany billing fails because the system cannot identify which customer represents the selling company code.

Select the row with Sales Org 1000, Dist.Channel 10, Division 00, and Plant 2000
Click Details magnifying glass

config_steps.step: Define Internal Intercompany Billing Document Type IV
config_steps.where: VOFA -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Billing > Billing Documents > Define Billing Types
config_steps.values: Billing Type: IV; Description: Intercompany Invoice; Number range: 54; Sign.ofIncompletion: 01; Acct Determination Procedure: KOFI00
config_steps.check: Create an intercompany invoice using VF01 with billing type IV and verify proper account posting.
config_steps.why: This billing type controls posting of the internal intercompany invoice from the supplying company code to the selling company code.
config_steps.if_missing: Without billing type IV, the system cannot generate internal intercompany invoices, stopping financial settlement between company codes.
actions: Enter /nVOFA in the command field and press Enter
Select billing type IV and click Details
Set Billing Type to IV and Description to Intercompany Invoice
Set Number range to 54
Set Sign.ofIncompletion to 01
Set Acct Determination Procedure to KOFI00
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign a customizing transport request

config_steps.step: Create Intercompany Pricing Condition Records for PI01
config_steps.where: VK11 -- Logistics > Sales and Distribution > Master Data > Conditions > Select Condition Type (e.g., PI01/PI02)
config_steps.values: Condition Type: PI01; Material: Intercompany Pricing Ref Material; Amount: Wholesale price; Currency: USD
config_steps.check: Create an intercompany invoice in VF01 and verify that condition PI01 prices the item with the correct wholesale amount.
config_steps.why: This master data provides the wholesale transfer price used when the supplying company bills the selling company.
config_steps.if_missing: If missing, intercompany invoices generate with zero value, causing financial discrepancies and failing FI postings.
actions: Enter /nVK11 in the command field and press Enter
Enter Condition Type PI01 and press Enter
Select key combination Sales Org. / Customer / Material and click Key Combination
Enter Sales Organization 1000, Customer C2000, and Intercompany Pricing Reference Material
Enter Wholesale price amount and Currency USD
Save (Ctrl+S) to create the condition record
